questions.topic: Computation in standard form, currency exchange and consumer arithmetic

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Determine the value of the following, giving your answer in standard form.

((47.5)^2 - 56.25)/sqrt(1.6 x 0.4)

criteria.description: the value of the expression
the value written in standard form

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The table below shows the rates of exchange at a cambio in Port of Spain.

US$1.00 = TT$6.80
EC$1.00 = TT$2.72

Using the table, calculate the EC equivalent of US$1.00.

criteria.description: finding the EC equivalent of TT$1.00
multiplying the EC equivalent of TT$1.00 by 6.80

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Kalifa's aunt in Saint Lucia sent her EC$1 250.00, which Kalifa exchanged for US dollars. Calculate the amount received in US dollars.

criteria.description: dividing by the EC equivalent of US$1.00

parts.label: (c) (i)
parts.prompt:
Kalifa's mobile telephone plan has a fixed charge of $45.00 per month, which includes 300 minutes of calls. Each additional minute is charged at $0.35. In January she made calls totalling 465 minutes.

Calculate the TOTAL amount that Kalifa paid for her telephone service for the month of January.
parts.solution: Kalifa made 465 - 300 = 165 minutes of calls beyond those included, and these cost 165 x $0.35 = $57.75. The total amount paid is $45.00 + $57.75 = $102.75.

criteria.description: finding the charge for the 165 additional minutes
the total amount paid

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: For the next month, February, Kalifa paid $136.00 for her telephone service. Determine the TOTAL number of minutes of calls that she made in February.
parts.solution: The charge for the additional minutes was $136.00 - $45.00 = $91.00, so the number of additional minutes is 91.00/0.35 = 260. Adding the 300 minutes included in the plan, Kalifa made 300 + 260 = 560 minutes of calls.

criteria.description: subtracting the fixed charge and dividing by the charge per additional minute
the total number of minutes

questions.stem: Anisha is investigating the sums of sequences of whole numbers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Anisha first added the odd numbers, starting at 1: the first 2 odd numbers, then the first 3, then the first 4, and so on. The first rows of the table are shown below. Some rows have not been included.

Study the pattern of numbers in each row of the table. Complete the table by filling in the missing information.
parts.solution: Each row adds the next odd number. The nth odd number is 2n - 1, so the 5th is 2(5) - 1 = 9 and the 9th is 2(9) - 1 = 17. The sum of the first n odd numbers is n^2, so the sum of the first 4 is 4^2 = 16, of the first 5 is 5^2 = 25, and of the first 9 is 9^2 = 81.

table.caption: The sums of the odd numbers.

s4.description: the sum of the first 4 odd numbers

s5.description: the sum of the first 5 odd numbers

s9.description: the sum of the first 9 odd numbers

ln.description: the nth odd number, in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
Anisha then added the EVEN numbers in the same way, and noted that

2 + 4 = 6 = 2 x 3
2 + 4 + 6 = 12 = 3 x 4
2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20 = 4 x 5.

Using the pattern derived from the 3 statements above, determine the value of 2 + 4 + 6 + ... + 30.
parts.solution: The last number 30 is the 15th even number, and the pattern gives the sum as 15 x 16 = 240.

criteria.description: recognises that 30 is the 15th even number
the sum, 240

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Hence, write a formula in terms of n for the sum 2 + 4 + 6 + ... + 2n.
parts.solution: Each statement is of the form n(n + 1), where 2n is the last number added. So 2 + 4 + 6 + ... + 2n = n(n + 1).

criteria.description: the formula in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.solution: The four regions account for every one of the 32 students, so (21 - x) + x + (17 - x) + 5 = 32. That is 43 - x = 32, so x = 43 - 32 = 11.

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: The actual distance between two villages on the island is 325 000 cm. What is this actual distance in km?

criteria.description: the actual distance in kilometres

parts.label: (c) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the ACTUAL area, in km^2, of the forest reserve, given that 1 x 10^10 cm^2 = 1 km^2.
parts.solution: The forest reserve covers 24 of the small squares, so its area on the map is 24 cm^2. The scale is 1 : 25 000, so 1 cm on the map represents 25 000 cm and 1 cm^2 on the map represents 25 000 x 25 000 = 625 000 000 cm^2. The actual area is therefore 24 x 625 000 000 = 15 000 000 000 cm^2, and since 1 x 10^10 cm^2 = 1 km^2 this is 1.5 km^2.

criteria.description: the area of the forest reserve on the map, in cm^2
1 cm^2 on the map represents 25 000 x 25 000 cm^2
the actual area, in km^2
